Kuvitus: huoneessa kaksi samankokoista i: Illustration: two balloons of the same size in a room. The helium balloon has risen to the ceiling with its string hanging down, and the ordinary balloon filled with air rests on the floor.
Kuvitus: kuumailmapallo leijuu järven yl: Illustration: a hot-air balloon floats above a lake. A burning flame above the basket heats the air inside the balloon.
Havainnekuva, hiukkaset suurennettuina j: Schematic picture with the particles enlarged: three containers of the same size at the same pressure and temperature, each with the same number of particles, that is, amount of substance n = 1.00 mol. The molar mass is 4.00 g/mol for helium, 29.0 g/mol for air and 44.0 g/mol for carbon dioxide. The bar under each container is the mass of the gas to scale: one mole weighs a different amount for different gases.
Havainnekuva, hiukkaset kuvattu suurenne: Schematic picture with the particles enlarged: two gas balloons of the same size at the same pressure and temperature. Both contain the same number of particles and the amount of substance n = 0.21 mol. The mass of the gas in the helium balloon is m = 0.83 g and in the air balloon m = 6.0 g, because the particles of air are heavier. The arrows show the motion of the particles to scale: at the same temperature the light helium particles move faster, and the length of the arrow is the ratio of the speeds, 2.7 : 1.
Kaavakuva neljästä männällä suljetusta k: Diagram of four gas cylinders closed with pistons, particles enlarged. From left to right: in the initial state the number of particles is N, the temperature is T and the volume is V, and the pressure is p. The pressure is 2p when there are twice as many particles (2N), when the temperature in kelvins is doubled (2T), that is, the particles move faster, or when the piston has been pushed to half the volume (V/2). The length of the arrows shows the speed of the particles.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kahden samanlaise: Graph to scale: the pressure p of the gas in two identical, closed and rigid containers as a function of the temperature T in kelvins when the containers are heated. Both series of measurements are straight lines. The points of gas A are (200 K; 50 kPa) and (400 K; 100 kPa), and the points of gas B are (200 K; 30 kPa) and (400 K; 60 kPa). The grid spacing is 100 K and 10 kPa.
